selected.title: Who checks the draft
selected.texas_link: A UTHealth Houston school post names UT Physicians and its plan, and Abridge announced an agreement with the University of Texas System's health AI initiative. The film draws a generic illustrated exam room and names no real clinic, clinician or patient.

movement.action: is working toward adopting Epic's ambient listening platform as one unified system after pilots of two other ambient AI products
movement.object: ambient AI that drafts clinical visit notes

selected.why_today: On October 8th, 2026 Abridge announced an enterprise agreement with University of Texas REAL Health AI, and a UTHealth Houston post dated September 9th, 2026 says UT Physicians is working toward Epic's ambient listening platform. These are two separate movements.
selected.consequence: A clinician is expected to review a draft note that software wrote from the visit, and no source measures how well that check works.
selected.application_change: Visit notes at UT health institutions can be drafted by AI from the conversation for a clinician to verify.
selected.counter_image: No source here gives a switch date, an accuracy measure or time saved. The Abridge figures are the vendor's own, and the school page doesn't say the Abridge agreement has been deployed.
selected.earned_take: The vendor's design and the statute's review condition both point the check at the clinician, and none of these sources says how well it works.

agency.next_step: UT Physicians has no published switch or completion date, and each UT health institution decides its own use under the framework.
agency.who_can_act: UT Physicians and McGovern Medical School leadership, the leaders of each UT health institution, and the Texas Medical Board, which the statute names as the source of the records standard.

filmability.viewer_question: When an AI listens to a Texas doctor's visit and drafts the note, who checks it before it goes in the record?
filmability.opening_action: An illustrated exam room where a conversation becomes a draft line on a note screen, disclosed as Illustration.
filmability.mechanism: Input: the spoken visit. Transformation: software drafts the note and, per the vendor, links each line to source data. Result: the clinician verifies the draft, and Texas law conditions AI diagnostic use on practitioner review of all AI-created records. Limit: none of these sources says how well the check works.
filmability.human_consequence: Physicians who review the drafts and the patients whose visits are the source. No person is named and no outcome is claimed.
filmability.source_limit: The Abridge figures and design claims are the vendor's own. The school page gives no date, accuracy or time figure. The statute is written around diagnosis, and its text doesn't say whether a visit note counts. No footage of any Texas exam room exists in the sources.
